0.content:
Rene and Jakob founded the secret society in Fontaine more than 400 years ago. It aimed to use the power of the Primordial Sea to fuse many wills into one being and so survive the prophesied destruction. It met at the Tower of Ipsissimus, was later declared an illegal extremist group and had its tower sealed. Members held clearance levels from one to four.

After the Ordo's collapse, its leader, the Master, remained in the Primordial Sea. The Ordo also clashed violently with Mary-Ann at Elynas, which ended in her death.

1.content:
Rene's calculation, built from Khaenri'ahn records, that predicted the drying of the world's waters and, after centuries, a second flood. He believed no new civilization could rise afterwards. Alain did not believe it. The Master later used the formula to create the Doomsday Clock.

Rene needed outside "variables" to change the result, which led him to Abyssal power, to the Descender idea and to the ancient method of the Golden Troupe.

2.content: Rene's closest friend, whom he met in childhood. Jakob nearly died during their travels; Rene saved him with Abyssal power and turned him into a "neohuman" who can take the form of an Iniquitous Baptist. Jakob then helped design the Ordo's rituals and later built the vessel that housed Rene's consciousness.

3.comment: Rene de Petrichor: Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin
3.content: Childhood friends from the Narzissenkreuz Institute. Alain refused Rene's requests for help, and Rene says he does not blame him. Mary-Ann made Rene happy simply by being near. Both refused to join the Ordo.

4.comment: Rene de Petrichor: Rene's Investigation Notes
4.content: Rene's notes, found in the Sumeru quest "As the Khvarena's Light Shows", record his research on Khvarena and the Gaokerena; torn "Pages From Some Lost Notes" in the Khaenri'ahn ruins under Gavireh Lajavard compare Khvarena, Azosite and the Abyss. The Enigmatic Pages found in Fontaine and the Fell Dragon's Monocle artifact text, added later, tell the rest of his life.

5.comment: Rene de Petrichor: Rene's legacy in Nod-Krai
5.content: In the 6.3 Archon Quests "Tracing the Footsteps of the Past" and "The First Sliver of Moonlight", Sandrone (the Marionette) studies Rene's draft lectures and records and Alain's old notes on him. She says Alain despised Rene's theories but never found better alternatives, so she adopted some of Rene's ideas, and that Rene "once foretold the fate of the world", probably using the Primordial Sea. She ran into problems implementing his Four Orthants theory, and observes that his world-formula, full of constants, shows he thought the world's fate predetermined. The Knave, surprised, asks whether Alain and Rene were not "mortal enemies".

6.content: During the limited-time 6.7 event "Sunny Summer Fontinalia" (quest "Those We Have Lost"), Sandrone explains that Rene devised soul-severing as the first step towards letting souls live on forever and so saving the world. His imperfect Four Orthants theory caused a failure that dissipated his physical form; Jakob, trying to restore him, severed the souls of people who stood in his way. Souls severed after Rene awoke merged into his consciousness, but the earlier ones were left wandering Fontaine's waters and in time became corrupted. Sandrone, who never knew Rene, deals with them because Alain regretted not helping his friend and wished to mend things with him. She also shows a photo of Alain and Rene at the Institute of Natural Philosophy from before their falling-out.
